# Lines, layout and swaps

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Lines that build, make room, re-centre and swap words in place, and the layouts type sits in. 44 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Accelerating payoff cadence

`ty-accelerating-payoff-cadence` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any · also `dv-accelerating-swap-run`

The words of the payoff arrive faster and faster, each one quicker than the last, so the line tightens into its last word.

- **Build:** Words cadence="accelerate" (gaps shrink geometrically from the stagger to accelTo x it, house 0.5; each word's fade shortens with its gap), accent on the last word (accentOn="last"). For lists and montages use the house gap tables: cadence={ACCEL.rows} (18, 18, 14, 10, 8, 6, 6 f@60) or ACCEL.montage. One tick per onset drives the sound; a rest beat follows the payoff.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`, `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Gaps from the stagger (12 f@60 calm) down to half of it; rows 9, 9, 7, 5, 4, 3, 3 at 30 fps.
- **Use when:** The last fragment before a reveal, a checklist completing, a montage speeding into the end.
- **Avoid when:** Calm reading lines in the body of the film: one accelerating run per act at most.

### Animated line re-break

`ty-line-rebreak-glide` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A centred one-line statement re-breaks into a two-line stack, or back, with every word gliding from its old slot to its new one, so the layout changes without a cut or a jump.

- **Build:** Pre-solve both layouts with measureTracked and baselineOf. Layout A is one centred line; layout B is two centred lines at pitch = lead x size, the block centred on the same point, optionally at a smaller size s_B. Store each word's centre in both. Move each word i as one FLIP: p_i = prog(f, s + 2i, s + 2i + D_i, E.glide), with D_i = clamp(0.15 x travel_i, 30, 48) f; x = mix(xA_i, xB_i, p_i); scale = lmix(1, s_B / s_A, p_i). Give y its own curve, mix(yA_i, yB_i, arrive(prog(f, s + 2i - 4, s + 2i - 4 + D_i, E.outSoft))), so words that change rows drop first and slide second and never pass through a neighbour. Keep travel under 320 px per word: E.glide peaks at about 3x its mean speed, so D = 0.15 x travel holds readable words near 20 px/f (render the blurred master). If a word would travel further, split the line differently or cut. When an insert causes the re-break (an icon popping into a gap), start it 6 f after the insert lands; once settled, drift the block at 0.3 px/f.
- **Timing:** Per word, D = 0.15 x travel, clamped to 30-48 f, on E.glide (peak about 20 px/f, near 30% of the move). y leads x by 4 f on E.outSoft through arrive. Stagger 2 f in the reading order of the new layout. Travel at most 320 px. Starts 6 f after a causing insert. Settled drift 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** An inserted icon or a longer word makes a centred line too wide. A headline must stack to free half the frame for a product shot. Returning a stacked headline to a single line for the payoff.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 7 words. Re-breaks that carry the hero word far from where it was being read (keep it as the still anchor). More than one re-break per statement. Vertical formats, where a stack is already the default layout.

### Blur-swap rescale

`ty-blur-swap-rescale` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A big word blurs out and instantly re-forms smaller as the start of the full line, so the type changes scale without a rubbery size tween.

- **Build:** Use two layers and never animate font-size. Old layer: q = prog(f, s, s + 6, E.in), blur = blurOut(q, 12), scale x lmix(1, 0.85, q), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same 6 f, still moving in its current direction. New layer from s + 2: p = prog(f, s + 2, s + 16, E.out), scale = lmix(1.25, 1, p), blur = blurIn(p, 12), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; carry any ongoing drift so both layers travel at the same px/f. Optional tracking collapse on the new line: letter-spacing +0.25 em -> the token's tracking over 16 f on E.out, so the small word arrives spread wide and slams together.
- **Timing:** Old out 6 f (E.in, blurOut 12 px); new in 14 f from +2 f (E.out, blurIn 12 px, scale 1.25 -> 1, edges of a 1000 px line about 51 px/f on frame 1); 4 f overlap; typical cap-height change -35%; tracking collapse 16 f E.out.
- **Use when:** Going from one or two giant words to the full readable sentence; right after tr-giant-word-punch-out; any big-to-small type handoff inside one continuous take.
- **Avoid when:** As a default between unrelated lines (it is not a crossfade substitute); small-to-small swaps; overlaps longer than 10 f, which read as a dissolve.

### Line moves through: arrive, drift, leave as one move

`dv-through-move-line` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

A line enters already moving (77 px/f) and decelerating, drifts at a constant slow speed while it is read, and leaves on an expo-in: one continuous move, never parked; a card can shrink fast-slow-fast and cut at the fastest point; a label can recede steadily like it is moving away; the frame can contract a few px a side during a silent hold.

- **Build:** Words (rise from the side) + a drift transform + exit 'launch'. Anatomy: Expo-out arrival, linear drift (0.3 %/f or a few px/f), expo-in exit; a receding label shrinks to 0.59x over 2 s. Sound: A sub-bass hit on the arrival; silence under the contraction.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Arrival 20-30 f, drift for the read, exit 14-20 f.
- **Use when:** Openers, statements between scenes, loops (elements already moving on the first frame).
- **Avoid when:** Parking the line between its entrance and exit.

### Line re-centres on a long exponential

`dv-recentre-glide` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

The line keeps re-centring on a long soft exponential while words arrive (each sliding in a little from the right, or rising into place), so the whole line drifts to its centre as one tween.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="glide"> (E.expo, recentreDur 46). Anatomy: Left edge decaying about 0.75 a frame; the line itself sliding in 150-275 px from the right while words rise every 7 f; an appended half arrives grey and darkens in 3 f. Sound: Chat pop or voice phrase onsets.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** Re-centre 30-60 f (t50 0.17 s, t90 0.47 s); words 14-18 f each, 6-14 f apart.
- **Use when:** Calm, speech-paced lines; a second half appended after a pause.
- **Avoid when:** Fast builds (the glide lags behind the words).

### Line re-centres with most of the move on frame one

`dv-recentre-jump` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

When a word is appended to a centred line, the whole line jumps 44-88 % of the way to its new centre on the very frame the word appears and eases the rest; nothing slides under a word being read. A small icon can anchor the line and ride along.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="jump"> (22 f on E.jump). Anatomy: First-frame share 55-84 % (house 66 % in the first 30 fps frame), the rest over 3-8 frames; the first frames may carry a short horizontal smear; variant: the pair re-centres in exactly one frame; variant: a stacked block of lines re-centres 6 f after each addition. Sound: Word onsets.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** 10-24 f in all; first-frame speed 21-77 px/f.
- **Use when:** Every centred build line; captions appended word by word to the voice.
- **Avoid when:** A slow glide under a word being read; jumping before the word exists.

### Make room in one frame

`ty-make-room-jump` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any · also `dv-make-room-creep-jump`

A held line creeps, then jumps most of the way in a single frame to open room for the next word, and settles; the new word cuts on in the open space.

- **Build:** <LineSnap mode="room" held="You're" word="scaling" room={{ start }} /> or, in a chain, <Chain recentre="room" ink="pop" />. makeRoomState() creeps 0.28 s (17 % of the distance, speed rising), covers 67.5 % on one frame, settles over 0.24 s; the jump frame is declared (one stepped frame) so it is never shutter-blurred. The new word shows on the jump frame (wordAt / the fragment's first frame). As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'room', text, at }}>` (the held words creep, cover 67.5 % in one declared frame, the last word cuts on in the room).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/LineSnap`, `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** Creep 0.2-0.4 s, jump 60-75 % in one frame, tail 0.2-0.3 s; one per line at most.
- **Use when:** A statement whose next word is the point: the room appearing is the emphasis.
- **Avoid when:** Every fragment of a chain (use the jump re-centre); lines that would travel more than about 300 px.

### One word set apart in the line

`dv-one-word-emphasis` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

One word of a line is set heavier, or in the accent, from the moment it appears; ranked rows can carry medal tones on their numerals.

- **Build:** Words with a span override (accentOn index, or a weight). Anatomy: Weight step (regular to semibold or bold), or the accent colour; medal tones only on rank numerals. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Static.
- **Use when:** The key word of a closing line; the top three of a ranking.
- **Avoid when:** More than one emphasised word per line.

### Only the last word swaps

`dv-slot-word-swap` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

A held line keeps its start and swaps only its last word, several times ("for writers / editors / teams"): the outgoing word heats in colour while the line creeps, the swap lands with two big frames and a settle; small camera nudges alternate direction with each swap.

- **Build:** <LineSnap mode="room"> for the creep-jump plus a slot that HardSteps the word; colour heat via HueSweep back. Anatomy: Creep 1, 2, 6 px/f; swap; two big frames; settle; variant: the last word rolls vertically while gap tiles turn into icons. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LineSnap`
- **Timing:** Swap 20-30 f; nudges 26-32 f in-out; roll 8 f.
- **Use when:** Listing audiences, use cases or outcomes in one held sentence.
- **Avoid when:** More than three or four swaps.

### Re-centring line build

`ty-recentre-line-build` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any · also `dv-chain-build-recentre`

Fragments join a centred line; on the very frame a new word shows, the line jumps most of the way to its new centre, so the new word arrives in open space and never slides sideways.

- **Build:** Write the thought as a COPY build chain (timeline.ts chain('id', 'build', ...)) and draw it with <Chain chain="id" recentre="jump" />: the re-centre runs on E.jump over 22 f@60 from the fragment's first frame (42 % in the first 60 fps frame, 66 % in the first 30 fps frame), the read words ride it, the arriving fragment stays put. For a printed look add ink="partial" (part-inked words filling in over 10 f@60) or ink="pop" (cut on at full ink). 'slot' opens the room 12 f@60 early when the new words should rise into a still slot; 'glide' is the old exponential glide. chainJumps() gives the move frames for sound and the layout audit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** Jump 22 f@60 (normal: 55-84 % of the move in the first 30 fps frame, the rest in 3-8 frames; a softer 50 % first frame: recentreDur about 40 f@60); a new fragment every 1-1.5 s on the calm pace.
- **Use when:** Any centred line that builds over two or more fragments; statements, stat rows, typed headlines.
- **Avoid when:** Left-aligned layouts (no re-centre); moves over about 280 px per fragment (split the line).

### Small plain caption directly on the picture

`dv-plain-caption-on-picture` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

A short white sans caption (cap 2.3-2.8 % of the frame) sits centred on live footage or a photo's mid-tone, no box, no shadow, no scrim; the picture's shallow depth of field keeps it legible.

- **Build:** <Words> with no entrance (cut-on) at caption size over <Footage>/<Photo>. Anatomy: Centred, thin to regular weight, slight negative tracking. Sound: The voice; the caption already on screen at the first syllable.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Present from the cut; held per tagline.
- **Use when:** Voice-locked subtitles; taglines over a photo.
- **Avoid when:** Busy, sharp backgrounds behind the caption.

### The gap opens before the word arrives

`dv-make-room-early` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

The line starts sliding 3-6 frames before the next word (or avatar, or version token) appears, so the gap is already open when it lands; the newcomer can pop in at the slide's peak speed or shove the previous word aside.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="slot" recentreLead={10}>. Anatomy: Lead 3-6 f; the token appears at peak slide speed; a shove of 70 px in 2 blurred frames plus a 3 f settle; an icon pushed back in two pushes. Sound: The token on a kick (+39 ms); a note or click on the avatar pop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** Lead 6-12 f at 60 fps; slides 30-80 f quint-out.
- **Use when:** Builds where the new element is visual (an avatar, a token, an icon).
- **Avoid when:** Opening the gap so early that it reads as a mistake (over 8 f).

### Vertical word stack

`ty-vertical-word-stack` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · vertical

In a tall frame each new word lands on its own line under the last while the stack rises one line, so the newest word always sits on the optical centre.

- **Build:** Line pitch 1.05x the font size (110-140 px statement type in 9:16), lines left- or centre-aligned inside safeBox() so the stack clears the feed zones. Word k lands at land_k: translateY +0.35 em -> 0 on arrive(prog(f, land_k, land_k + 18, E.out)), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; the stack container moves up by the sum over k of pitch x spr(f, land_k, SPR.firm), peaking at about 11 px/f for a 150 px pitch. Lines more than two steps old fade out through a feathered top mask (mask-image transparent -> opaque over the top 0.8 pitch), so at most 3 words of one statement are on screen; the final word may arrive in the accent and relax to ink.
- **Timing:** A word every 24-30 f; word rise 18 f E.out; stack step SPR.firm (97% in 27 f); at most 3 lines visible; final hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word with a 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** Vertical cut-downs where a horizontal line would be too small; speaking-pace statements on a phone-sized frame; one word per beat.
- **Avoid when:** 16:9 masters (use ty-recentre-line-build); statements over 6 words; stacking two separate statements.

### Hero word shrinks in hard scale steps

`dv-hard-scale-steps` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting

A hero word shrinks from 3.3x to rest in a few hard scale cuts with 0-2 frame holds and no tween (3.32 -> 1.71 -> 1.045 -> 1.0).

- **Build:** HardStep on scale. Anatomy: Steps on single frames, each about half the remaining scale. Sound: Key-click transients on the steps.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** 10 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A word arriving on key-click transients.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth films.

### Old line pushes up and dims in one frame

`dv-old-line-push-dim` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · any

When the second line arrives, the first moves up on a fast S-curve and drops to about a third of its strength in a single frame.

- **Build:** Words move on E.strongInOut + HardStep opacity. Anatomy: Move 111 px; opacity step 1 -> 0.36 on one frame. Sound: A kick.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Move 28 f (peak 39 px/f); dim 1 f.
- **Use when:** Two-line statements where the second line is the point.
- **Avoid when:** Keeping both lines at full strength.

### Old line shrinks out, new line swaps in large

`dv-scale-out-swap-in` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · any

The old line shrinks a little on an ease-in, then on one frame the new line replaces it at 104-108 % and eases down to size: a swap with a breath.

- **Build:** Words exit 'launchFade' on scale + Oversize from 1.08 on the swap frame. Anatomy: Shrink to 95.6 %, hard swap, 108 % -> 100 % ease-out. Sound: A whoosh pair, or on the beat.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Oversize`
- **Timing:** Out 14-20 f, in 20 f, swap 0 f.
- **Use when:** Status lines, a title swapping to a tagline.
- **Avoid when:** Big scale ranges (keep it under 10 %).

### One huge word fills the panel and pushes in

`dv-hero-word-push` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

One key verb alone fills the panel (15-19 % of its height) and pushes in +24 % on an expo-out.

- **Build:** Words + camera push (E.snapOut, +24 %). Anatomy: Single word, push on expo-out. Sound: On the swap after the zoom.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 28 f.
- **Use when:** The verb of the claim, after a zoom-through.
- **Avoid when:** Two words.

### Re-centre jumps on its own cadence

`dv-recentre-stepped` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A growing lockup or caption re-centres in one-frame jumps (about half a letter width) on a different cadence from the letters landing (jumps every 8 f, letters every 6 f), creeping between jumps; the re-centre can lead the word's resolve by 6 f.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="jump" recentreDur={1}> inside <Stepped fps={7.5}> for the line, letters on their own grid via hotGlyphState. Anatomy: Jumps of 11-83 px; creep 2-3 px/f between; on twos for a stepped look. Sound: None of its own.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`, `fx/Stepped`
- **Timing:** Jumps every 8 f; letters every 6 f; two 2-frame moves of 20 px.
- **Use when:** Logo lockups built letter by letter; stepped, graphic films.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth films.

### Sentence lands with a ribbon tail

`dv-ribbon-tail-sentence` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

After a whip cut the sentence is still travelling and each later word sits progressively lower and later, so the line lands like a ribbon settling from its head.

- **Build:** Words with stagger 2-3 f and rise growing per index (rises[]), carried from the whip speed. Anatomy: Per-word delay and a vertical offset growing with the index; the head word lands first. Sound: The cut on a hit (+48 ms).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 45 f expo-out; the second word half-way at 5 f.
- **Use when:** The first line after a whip.
- **Avoid when:** Long sentences.

### The last word snaps the line larger

`ty-last-word-snap` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical · also `dv-line-scale-snap`

On the frame the payoff word lands the whole line jumps about 2.2x larger in one frame; the read words settle a few pixels and a short defocus clears while the new word fades in.

- **Build:** <LineSnap mode="snap" held="You Can" word="Now" snap={{ at }} origin="left" /> or snapLast on Chain / Words. House: x2.2, settle 31 px (1080p) on E.glideOut over 7 f@30, defocus 3.1 px on a half cosine over 7 f@30 (at most two ladder copies), new word 16 % -> 100 % over 5 f@30 with an 11 px rise. The snap frame is declared. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'snap', text, at }}>` (the read words at 1/2.2, the last word lands with one declared x2.2 frame).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/LineSnap`, `fx/Chain`, `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** One frame of snap; everything settled within about 0.25 s.
- **Use when:** The last word of a statement or a launch line: the payoff.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; small type that would still be small after the snap.

### Two type voices with fixed jobs

`dv-two-type-voices` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · any

A film gives two faces two jobs: statements in a high-contrast display face, UI in a small grotesk; a wide bold title face for one act and a light weight for the next; big caps with a tiny connector word between them.

- **Build:** Two font roles in brand/tokens; Words for statements, kit Text for UI. Anatomy: Size contrast 3-5x between the voices; the display face never appears inside UI. Sound: None.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Two weights and widths of the brand family (heavy display, light UI). The full look relies on serif, italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Static choice; the connector word can type while the caps fade.
- **Use when:** Editorial launches; films with an act structure.
- **Avoid when:** More than two voices; a second face that fights the brand.

### Word cuts on touching, then the space opens

`dv-space-opens-after` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Each appended word cuts on with no word space (the line reads run-together for a frame or two), then the spaces open and the line re-centres: the word visibly docks.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="jump"> with a word-space tween from 0 to the font space over 8 f (letter-spacing on the gap span). Recipe: each word's margin-left = space x k with k 0 -> 1 over 12 f (cubic out); negative start values give the overlap version. Anatomy: Spaces open over 3-4 f; re-centre 65-68 % in the first frame, x0.7 a frame after. Sound: One soft tick per word (±45 ms). Materials: Tight append: the new word lands touching the previous one (zero word space, or even overlapping it when it flies in large, glyphs compositing darker where they cross); over the next 8-16 f only the newcomer slides right and the normal space opens on an ease-out while earlier words stay put (left-aligned lines), or the line re-centres once the colour has cooled from the accent to ink. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'open', text, at }}>` (each word soft for its first frames and in the accent, the space opening in 7 f, the line re-centring on E.jump with a trail).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/Chain`
- **Materials:** Tight append: the new word lands touching the previous one (zero word space, or even overlapping it when it flies in large, glyphs compositing darker where they cross); over the next 8-16 f only the newcomer slides right and the normal space opens on an ease-out while earlier words stay put (left-aligned lines), or the line re-centres once the colour has cooled from the accent to ink.
- **Timing:** Spaces 7-8 f; re-centre about 24 f.
- **Use when:** Taglines built word by word; a brand line.
- **Avoid when:** Long words that become unreadable when run together.

### Words land from four directions

`dv-kinetic-stack-directions` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting

On grid paper, lines and words land with an expo-out from left, right, top and bottom in turn, with a small arrow: a kinetic poster.

- **Build:** Words with a per-word rise direction, stagger 6 f. Anatomy: Entries 2-4 f apart, each from a different side, 15 f each. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 33 f in all.
- **Use when:** Poster-style title cards.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films.

### Braces jump apart and the words swap inside

`dv-brace-jump-insert` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, feature, sting

To insert or swap a word between braces, the closing brace jumps outward one frame before the new word cuts on (59-73 % of its travel in that frame); for a swap, the braces accelerate apart during the last 0.4 s of the hold and the words change exactly at peak velocity.

- **Build:** Build: <Brackets phrases={[{ at, text }...]} x y font braceColor mode="insert"|"peak"> (fx/Brackets): insert: the closing brace jumps 66 % of its travel one frame before the word, then settles (10 f); peak: the braces run apart on an in-out (60 f) and the words swap on its fastest frame (a velocity seam). Anatomy: Braces are separate glyphs with their own motion; jump frame, expo settle (k 7-12); a 14 f drift; swap at the fastest frame. Sound: The audio onset with the word (-2 ms); the biggest hit (kick + sub-drop) on a swap.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Brackets`
- **Timing:** Settle 10-12 f; swap run 60 f (in-out with the peak at the swap).
- **Use when:** Swapping the key word of a held statement; code-like or product-like copy.
- **Avoid when:** Serif or decorative braces outside a supplied brand.

### Echo copies slide out from behind the word

`dv-echo-copies-knockout` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Copies of a word, each on its own solid knock-out box so the nearer copies hide the farther ones, slide out from behind the word in rings, then contract back.

- **Build:** Build: <EchoCopies at offset={{ x, y }} x y ground back={{ at }}>{word}</EchoCopies> (fx/Echoes): rings at +1, +3, +4 f (25 fps) slide out on E.snapOut over 27 f (half way in 0.05 s, 90 % in 0.2 s), each on a box of the ground's colour so nearer rings hide farther ones; contract back in 20 f. Anatomy: Rings at +1, +3, +4 f, each expo-out (t50 0.04 s, t90 0.20 s); contraction 20 f. Sound: The full bed enters on the drop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Echoes.EchoCopies`
- **Timing:** 72 f in all.
- **Use when:** A key word that should feel multiplied or scaled ("Scaling").
- **Avoid when:** Long words; more than once.

### Line opens a gap for an inline object

`dv-inline-gap-object` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A sentence splits between two words, the halves part and an object grows in the gap: an image chip that hard-cuts through several clips, a thumbnail that swaps content while the line reflows, or a pill that grows and types a sub-line.

- **Build:** Build: <InlineGap leftText rightText at gap h swaps={[...]} items={[...]}> (fx/InlineGap): the halves part on E.glideOut (16 f; up to 76 for a wide gap), the chip grows from a 3 px bar once the gap is a third open (7 f) and its content hard-cuts on swaps; close={{ at }} shuts the gap (5 f, E.buildIn); anchor="left" moves only the right half; halves lets each half arrive on its own. inlineGapFrames() for the cues. Anatomy: Halves part 44-410 px (expo, slow 4 f start); the object grows from a 1 px bar; content swaps inside on hard cuts; the line reflows and the block zooms up to x1.76. Sound: On the big hit; a toggle click on the pill. Materials: The object can be a photo-real character: a tiny dot in the word gap grows 6 -> 30 px in 6 f, then into a round white portrait (soft drop shadow) while the halves fly apart past the frame edges, blurring up to 25 px as the camera pushes; the portrait then rises into the next UI's header.
- **Primitive:** `fx/InlineGap`
- **Materials:** The object can be a photo-real character: a tiny dot in the word gap grows 6 -> 30 px in 6 f, then into a round white portrait (soft drop shadow) while the halves fly apart past the frame edges, blurring up to 25 px as the camera pushes; the portrait then rises into the next UI's header.
- **Timing:** Part 16-76 f; object grows 7-18 f; swaps every 6-20 f; reflow 10 f; squeeze 8 f.
- **Use when:** Showing what a word means ("[images]", "your [product]"); the product inside the copy.
- **Avoid when:** Gaps that break the read (split at a natural pause).

### Neighbouring words show as dim ghosts around the slot

`dv-ghost-reel` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

While a word sits in a slot, blurred dim copies of the previous and next words remain visible just outside the mask, like a slot-machine reel; a new line can cut in at 79 % defocused and grow while ghost copies spread above and below.

- **Build:** Build: <GhostReel n pitch swaps x y width slotH render> (fx/Reels): the slot sharp, the neighbours outside it through one fixed blur (6 px) at 20 %; each roll exits on E.buildIn (26 f) and settles on E.snapOut (16 f). Anatomy: Main word sharp in the slot; ghosts blurred, 10-25 % strength, moving with the roll; spreading ghosts on an ease-out. Sound: A kick on the swap.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Reels.GhostReel`
- **Timing:** Grow 56 f; ghosts 52 f ease-out; exit 40 f ease-in.
- **Use when:** Word swaps that should feel like a reel or a list; a line that is one of many.
- **Avoid when:** Ghosts strong enough to be read (keep them under 25 %).

### Phrase clamp at a junction

`ty-phrase-clamp-junction` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Two halves of a phrase arrive from opposite directions and lock on one baseline at a fixed junction, like a clamp closing.

- **Build:** Fix a junction (x about 48% of the frame, on the shared baseline): the first half is right-aligned to it and the second half left-aligned, both measured with measureTracked so the junction gap is exactly one word space. Vertical default: hold the first half alone for 1 f at +64 px (the pre-pose), then translateY +64 -> 0 on arrive(p), p = prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), while each word of the second half drops -40 -> 0 the same way, word i starting at s + 2i; give every piece opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f and blurIn(p, 8), because frame 1 moves about 20 px/f. Horizontal snap: the line cuts in at full strength with each half 35 px out from the junction, closes to 0.75 of the word space over 10 f on E.out, then eases back to the true gap over 18 f on E.outSoft (the one designed undershoot, never closing the space); calm variant: a 1.7x gap closes to 1x over 80 f on E.outSoft. Put the lock on a beat and give it one 1.5% scale punch with hitPulse(t, 1, 4).
- **Timing:** Vertical: 18 f E.out, 64 px and 40 px travel (peak 19.7 and 12.3 px/f on frame 1), 2 f word stagger, 1 f pre-pose, opacity 3 f. Snap: 35 px per side over 10 f E.out (about 20 px/f on frame 1) to 0.75 of the gap, back over 18 f E.outSoft. Calm close: 80 f E.outSoft. Hold the locked line at least 54 f with a 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** A two-part claim whose halves mean more together (subject + promise, problem + fix); the payoff line; a junction that a slot roller will reuse.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over 5 words or halves of very unequal length; more than once per film; the end lockup.

### Slot roller beside a fixed phrase

`ty-slot-roller-fixed-phrase` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, vertical

A fixed phrase holds still while the word in its slot rolls through alternatives one line at a time, speeding up until the last one lands.

- **Build:** The fixed phrase sits in its own layer and never moves; the slot is a column of alternatives aligned to the junction, line pitch 1.5x the font size, translated by -index x pitch and cut by a feathered mask-image (transparent beyond +-1.2 pitch, opaque within +-0.5 pitch) so neighbours show only as slivers. Each step rolls on E.whip over 20 f (peak about 0.18 x pitch per frame, 12 px/f at a 68 px pitch); above a 110 px pitch, stretch the step to 0.18 x pitch frames so the rolling word stays at or under 20 px/f; the row on the junction baseline is ink and every other row is C.mute at no more than 1.3:1 contrast, flipped binary when |rowY - baselineY| < pitch/2 (no colour tween). For a run of 5 or more items, accelerate: intervals 26, 14, 12, 8, 8, 4, 4 f, where intervals under 12 f are whole-frame swaps chosen by fd(f) with no tween, the final item rolls home on SPR.detent, and every step gets a tick. For a loop, make the last item equal the first and wrap the index modulo the list.
- **Timing:** Step 20 f E.whip (0.18 x pitch frames above a 110 px pitch) every 29-34 f (0.48-0.57 s), 3 steps, then a 28 f hold before the cut. Accelerating run: 26/14/12/8/8/4/4 f (7 items in 76 f), last item on SPR.detent (home in about 9 f), held at least 54 f under a 0.3 px/f line drift. Pitch 1.5x the font size; ticks at least 3 f apart.
- **Use when:** One sentence frame that fits many subjects or capabilities; listing use-cases without spending screen time; a feature loop that cycles items.
- **Avoid when:** Items of very different widths in a centred layout (the fixed phrase would have to move); more than about 7 items; any mask loose enough that the neighbours read as a list.

### Type cut into strips that slide apart

`dv-strip-slice-type` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting

A number and a word are cut into horizontal strips (8-10 per glyph) that slide sideways at different offsets until they span the full width.

- **Build:** Build: <Slices kind="strips" at x y w h n={9}>{type}</Slices> (fx/Slices): each strip a clipped copy sliding sideways by a seeded share of the frame width on E.jump (spread by 3 f at 24 fps; 43 f); back={{ at }} gathers them. Anatomy: Strips with seeded offsets, expanding sideways; full width by 3 frames in. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Slices`
- **Timing:** 43 f.
- **Use when:** A big number becoming a field; a transition out of a stat.
- **Avoid when:** Text that must stay readable.

### Words hop between grid cells

`dv-grid-hop-words` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Words on small label boxes move one or two grid cells at a time, alternating axes like Manhattan routes, then all jump into the final sentence in one frame.

- **Build:** Build: <GridHop words={[{ path: manhattan(from, to), at }]} origin texts font box final={{ at, positions: sentencePositions(texts, x, y, font) }}> (fx/Echoes): one cell per hop on the stepped progress 0, .19, .36, .78, .95, 1 (9 f), axes alternating, then every word jumps into the sentence on one frame. Anatomy: Hops of 120 px on 16 fps steps (progress 0, 0.19, 0.36, 0.78, 0.95, 1); the final jump is one frame. Sound: Plastic clicks on the hops; a big click on the final jump.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Echoes.GridHop`
- **Timing:** Each hop 8-10 f; run 75 f; final jump 1 f.
- **Use when:** A sentence assembled from parts; layout tools, grids, editing products.
- **Avoid when:** Long sentences.

### Caption in the subject's negative space

`lc-negative-space-caption` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Each camera move ends on a pose where the product covers about two-thirds of the frame and leaves a clean band of empty stage, and the caption builds inside that band.

- **Build:** Design each anchor-camera end Shot (src/lib/camera.ts) so the subject covers 65-75% of the frame and leaves a clear 25-30% band on the side it turns away from (a right band when yawed left, a top band when pitched down); check the subject's corners with toScreen. Set the caption in that band: at most 24% of the frame width, 2-3 words per line, left-aligned, inset 8-10% from the frame edge and inside SAFE. Start its Words reveal in the last 25% of the camera move, or within 6 f of landing, so type and camera settle as one gesture; fade it out as a block before the camera moves again.
- **Timing:** Caption starts at 75% of the move, or within 6 f of landing; Words stagger 8 f, dur 26 f. Block exit 12-16 f on E.smooth, ending as the next move starts. Camera moves on E.cam.
- **Use when:** Single-take product walkthroughs and 3D UI slabs where each feature gets one pose and one caption; any shot where text laid over the UI would fight it.
- **Avoid when:** The subject must stay full-frame to be legible (caption above or below it instead), or a 9:16 frame, where the band should be top or bottom only.

### Left-aligned stack builds downward beside the product

`dv-left-stack-build` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature

Beside a tilted phone, a top-anchored left-aligned stack builds line by line every 5-7 f, each line rising about 50 px from a third strength.

- **Build:** <Words> per line with starts 12 f apart, left-aligned. Anatomy: Left margin about 158 px; lines added below; the last line in the accent. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Lines 10-14 f apart; each 30 f.
- **Use when:** Feature lists next to a device.
- **Avoid when:** Centred stacks next to off-centre products.

### Live cause-and-effect split

`lc-live-split-view` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature

Two panels share the frame side by side, the cause on one side (a chat, a list, an input) and the effect on the other (a generated page, a photo, a result), both live, while the camera creeps in.

- **Build:** Lay out two panels inside SAFE at 40/60 (the cause narrower), separated by a 3% W gutter, both the full height of the safe box and aligned on the same top edge; render the composition at 2x so a slow push stays sharp. Keep both sides moving: the cause streams text or steps (a typed reply, a marker hopping down a list) and the effect updates on the frame each cause completes (sections drawing in, or an image swapping on the marker's frame with a small kick of rotateY = 12 deg * hitPulse(f - s, 1, 2.5)). Push the world container linearly by about +0.017%/f, then leave on an accelerating pan (E.in over the last 40 f) and cut on its fastest frame, at most 60 px/f.
- **Timing:** Hold 180-240 f. Creep about +0.017%/f (+4% over 4 s) on E.linear. Swaps every 54 f with a 6 f settle. Exit pan 40 f on E.in, cut at the peak (at most 60 px/f).
- **Use when:** Showing that an input produces an output (prompt to page, list to detail, setting to preview), where seeing both at once is the point.
- **Avoid when:** Phone-first or vertical films (stack the two instead), or when either side's text would drop under 24 px at 1080p.

### The tagline is set as a string inside the product UI

`dv-copy-inside-ui` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, update

The line of copy is not laid over the UI: it is a real string inside it (the subtitle of the top result, a field's text, a notification) at UI size, typed by the same typing primitive as the rest of the film and marked only by being the one line in a second voice.

- **Build:** Recipe: put the copy into the UI mock's data and animate it with TypeOn or Chain. Anatomy: One metadata string replaced by the copy; marked by a second type voice or the accent; it continues by typing later in the shot. Sound: Key ticks, if any.
- **Timing:** Present from the row's arrival; highlighted about 52 f; the continuation typed in about 30 f.
- **Use when:** Update films and UI-led launches, where overlaid copy would fight the UI.
- **Avoid when:** Lines longer than the field; UI sizes that become illegible in vertical.

### Vertical clear-band stack

`lc-vertical-band-stack` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy any · vertical

In a 9:16 frame, the caption and the subject stack vertically inside the band the feed leaves clear, with their combined mass centred on that band rather than on the frame, and nothing important under the bottom caption zone or the right action rail.

- **Build:** Get the band from safeBox('feed9x16', W, H): 896 x 1230 px at 1080x1920, centred near y = 885. Stack inside it: the caption on top (fitSize to the band width, at most two lines), a 48 px gap, then the subject below (a UI card at 0.86 of the band width, or a phone screen cropped to its key region), with the stack's combined height centred on the band's cy. Moves are vertical: the subject rises 120 px into place through arrive(prog(f, a, a + 40, E.glide)), the caption reveals with Words 8 f later, and scene changes flow upward (the old stack exits up on E.in over 16 f while the new one rises from below). Never place things side by side, and check every frame with the layout audit so nothing crosses the feed zones.
- **Timing:** Subject rises 120 px over 40 f on E.glide; caption Words (stagger 8 f, dur 26 f) start 8 f after the subject; exits 16 f on E.in; hold 60-90 f per stack.
- **Use when:** Any vertical cut-down or vertical-first film for feeds.
- **Avoid when:** 16:9 masters (use a side-by-side composition there), or full-bleed moments where one giant word fills the screen anyway.

### Words part for an inserted object

`lc-gap-open-insert` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Inside a finished line, the words slide apart to open a gap and an object pops into it (an icon, a photo, a token, or a caret that grows into a container), so the sentence becomes a frame for the object.

- **Build:** Split the line into a left group, a slot and a right group. Animate the slot width w(f) from 0 to the object's width on prog(f, a, a + 16, E.glide), and move the groups with transforms (left translateX -w/2, right +w/2 for a centred line) rather than by reflowing flex widths. Pop the object into the slot once the gap is 70% open: scale 0 to 1 on spr(f, b, SPR.micro), with no overshoot. Container variant: a hairline caret grows to cap height, thickens into a capsule, then widens into the next UI element, pushing the words aside. Hold at least 14 f; to make the object the next scene, accelerate the groups apart on E.in over 16 f (faded, with blurOut) while the object scales up into the next shot's rect.
- **Timing:** Gap opens over 16 f on E.glide, which keeps a 200 px gap under 20 px/f per side. Object pop 6 f on SPR.micro. Hold 14-60 f. Exit: words 16 f on E.in, object scale-up 8-20 f into the cut. Caret variant: grow 6 f, hold 8 f, thicken 14 f, widen 24-62 f.
- **Use when:** Making a sentence about the object literally contain it (a product photo in a claim, a lock icon beside 'private', a prompt box between two words); morphing a headline into the first UI element of the next scene.
- **Avoid when:** Long lines whose parted words would leave the frame unintentionally, or an object that needs more room than a word gap can give (use a push-aside or a cut).

### Headline over a ghost of the UI

`lc-headline-over-ghost-ui` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A headline inks in from light grey to near-black while a faint copy of the product interface sits behind it, then the UI resolves to full strength as the headline leaves.

- **Build:** Use two layers: the product UI (a full-frame capture or live component) at opacity 0.15, and the headline centred on top of it. Ink the headline from C.mute to C.ink through mixColor on prog(f, a, a + 40, E.outSoft) (on a dark stage, C.mute to C.white). As the headline exits (Words with out, or a 16 f fade on E.smooth), raise the UI's opacity from 0.15 to 1 over 60 f on E.smooth with a slow scale from 1.03 to 1.0 on the same curve, so the next shot is already composed. If the UI is busy, defocus the ghost with RackFocus (t = 1, blur 10) and rack it sharp as it resolves.
- **Timing:** Ink resolve 40 f. Ghost UI at 10-20% opacity under the headline; it resolves to 100% over 60 f, starting when the headline's exit begins.
- **Use when:** Setting up a demo during a statement, so the move into the product needs no transition; a claim that names the product area about to be shown.
- **Avoid when:** High-contrast UIs whose ghost would muddy the type, or UI text at the same scale as the headline sitting directly behind it.

### Headline set so large the frame crops it

`dv-bleed-headline` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A light headline (ascenders 20 % of the frame height) runs off the right edge, its last letter half cut, while its words fade in and the frame drifts.

- **Build:** Words at a size wider than the frame, ink-in-place entrance. Anatomy: Static crop; words ink in place; drift under it. Sound: A breath swell; key-click ticks on word onsets.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Held 68 f.
- **Use when:** Openers on a misty plate; editorial covers.
- **Avoid when:** Cropping a letter that changes the word.

### Mark set as a word

`lc-mark-as-inline-word` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

A logo, partner mark or icon sits inside a sentence on the baseline at cap height, as if it were a word, appearing with its own delayed fade or swapping with a word in the same slot.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line with the mark in its own inline slot: height equal to the cap height from inkBox, bottom on the baseline, margin-left one space width (measureTracked(' ')), so the slot is reserved and nothing reflows. Reveal the words first (Words, stagger 8), then fade the mark in on its own about 17 f after the first word: opacity 0 to 1 on prog(f, s, s + 6, E.smooth), with no scale pop. To swap something in the slot, stack two spans: the outgoing one moves to translateY -8 px as it fades out while the incoming one rises from +8 px as it fades in, both over 8 f on E.ui.
- **Timing:** Mark appears about 17 f after the first word with a 4-6 f fade. Slot swap 8 f with 8 px travel. The line then drifts at 0.5 px/f.
- **Use when:** Co-branding inside a claim, naming a platform or integration without a separate logo slate, or turning a generic noun into the product name in place.
- **Avoid when:** Marks with fine detail or wide aspect ratios that cannot read at cap height, or the film's own final lockup, which appears once, at the end, on its own.

### Sentence placed around an object

`dv-words-around-object` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A sentence is distributed around a picture or card instead of sitting on one line: the first half top-left and the second bottom-right of a growing image cluster, words as tiles in the gaps of a masonry wall, one word above and one below the newest card riding its perspective, or one word cut on while a pull-back brings the other in from the frame edge.

- **Build:** Words placed in the object's coordinate space (inside its transform); pull-back via camera. Anatomy: Words placed on the object's corners or in its gaps; they share its plane and drift; the next card can occlude them. Sound: A fast air whoosh; a soft UI tap then silence.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Words 10 f apart; cut on with the card; pull-back -4.3 % in 2 f.
- **Use when:** When copy and imagery share a frame and the layout should feel designed.
- **Avoid when:** Read order that becomes ambiguous.

### Tiny labels in the empty corners

`dv-corner-micro-labels` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Three or four very small all-caps labels (10-12 px) and a contact line sit in the empty corners around a headline, arriving 1-2 frames apart and leaving with it.

- **Build:** Words at the ui role, pop entrance, staggered 4 f. Anatomy: Corner placement, all caps, tracked out. Sound: None. Materials: A tiny label decodes through random letters of the same width (2 + 2 + resolve, 10 f) as its tick dot appears under it.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Materials:** A tiny label decodes through random letters of the same width (2 + 2 + resolve, 10 f) as its tick dot appears under it.
- **Timing:** 3-5 f apart in; out with the line.
- **Use when:** Poster-like frames; an editorial end card.
- **Avoid when:** Labels that need reading (they are texture).

### Twin discs grow and hold words

`dv-twin-disc-words` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Two touching discs scale up on an expo-out and thin words appear inside them one at a time.

- **Build:** Cards springBox or enterState on two circles; Words inside. Anatomy: Discs about 180 px, touching; words at f+4, +7, +13. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Discs 16 f expo-out; words 6-12 f apart.
- **Use when:** A two-part idea (before / after, you / us).
- **Avoid when:** Long words that crowd the discs.

### Two words part around the subject, then converge

`dv-words-part-converge` · layout and composition · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Two caption words either side of the subject slide apart with an expo-out (the maximum split on the strongest kick), hold, then converge on an expo-in.

- **Build:** Two Words with mirrored x on E.snapOut, exit 'launch' toward each other. Anatomy: Split 180 px; 77 px/f first frame; hold; converge. Sound: Kick + sub-drop on the maximum split.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Part 28 f, hold 18 f, converge 24 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Framing a person or product with two words.
- **Avoid when:** Subjects that move a lot.
